Founder Jonathan Kumar is here asking our investors for $1 million dollars for his startup... Samaritan. Which Jonathan says can help solve homelessness.
Now conventional VC wisdom says that a successful startup is one that solves a real problem. And homelessness is a persistent one. More than half a million people were homeless last year. And that number has been ticking up. So it's a big deal.
But... is homelessness the kind of problem that venture capital can... or even should... solve?

So. There's a certain amount of money that's put on the beacon for donors in the last 30 days. The nonprofit says, hey good news, you have 50 bucks that's been donated to you. So how do they spend it?
But do consumers want this app? Do they want to get these notifications when they pass by? Or does it make them feel guilty every time they pass by if they don't give? How does that...?

Do you think this is... I'm just listening to this and here's my struggle. I love what you're doing and why you're doing it. I don't know if I want to capitalize on this. When I'm investing, I'm looking at it strictly as a return on investment. When I'm being charitable, I look at it as, how can I help and get the biggest impact? So this feels like it's in between. And that makes it challenging for me. Like I said, I really love your mission and what you're doing. But as a business, as a financial investment, I have to pass.
